name: Venda
notes: Venda (Tshivenḓa) — Bantu language of South Africa and Zimbabwe, one of South Africa's official languages. The Latin orthography adds five under-dot/circumflex-below letters (ḓ ḽ ṋ ṱ) for the dental series contrasting with the alveolar d l n t, and ṅ for /ŋ/ (⟨ng⟩ being prenasalised /ŋɡ/). Plain ⟨p t k ts tsh ṱ pf⟩ write the ejective series; the ⟨h⟩ digraphs write the aspirated series. Five vowels /i ɛ a ɔ u/, with close-mid allophones. Venda is tonal, but tone is not marked in the standard orthography and no tone marks are emitted.

sources.notes: UNVERIFIED BY A SECOND READER. The UNISA institutional repository was unreachable when this entry was checked, so the page images behind the claims below could not be opened independently. Re-check at https://uir.unisa.ac.za/handle/10500/17535 when that repository returns, and remove this paragraph once a second reader has seen the pages. §1.7 (pp. 14-17), read on the page image. The list on p. 15 gives the standard Tshivenda values this map uses: ⟨d⟩ voiced alveolar plosive, ⟨t⟩ ejective alveolar plosive, ⟨th⟩ aspirated alveolar plosive, ⟨n⟩ alveolar nasal, ⟨l⟩ alveolar lateral, and the under-circumflex dental series ⟨ḓ ṱ ṱh ṋ ḽ⟩ distinguished from the alveolars by the diacritic; the table on p. 17 places ⟨fh vh⟩ as bilabial fricatives, ⟨bv⟩ as a labiodental affricate, ⟨x⟩ velar and ⟨h⟩ glottal, ⟨ṅ⟩ velar nasal, and ⟨tsh dzh sh⟩ as prepalatal. Two limits: the work describes the Tshiguvhu dialect and gives the standard only for contrast, so the p. 17 table (where ⟨ts⟩ is both ejective and aspirated and ⟨tsh⟩ only aspirated) is Tshiguvhu and does not settle whether the standard's ⟨tsh⟩ is ejective as this map has it; and the p. 15 list calls ⟨ṱ⟩ a voiceless dental plosive without saying ejective, while the map writes t̪ʼ. The same list has a slip, giving ⟨l⟩ as both the alveolar tap and the alveolar lateral; the tap is ⟨r⟩.
